rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qafw means following, derived from the nape, and is metaphorically applied here to pursuing a claim or action.
rows.anchor: القفو : الاتباع ، يقال : قفاه يقفوه إذا اتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited object is an unsupported thought or allegation lacking evidence and even a preponderance of probability.
rows.anchor: الخاطر النفساني الذي لا دليل عليه ولا غلبة ظن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic people falsely attacked lineage, denying paternity from superficial resemblance or color while ignoring inherited traits across ancestors and prenatal influence.
rows.anchor: منها خلة من خلال الجاهلية ، وهي الطعن في أنساب الناس ، فكانوا يرمون النساء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Bedouin questioned a dark-skinned newborn's paternity; the Prophet compared inherited color to a dark camel in a gray herd and forbade disowning the child.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلعل ابنك نزعه عرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People also accused neighbors of adultery without witnessing it, especially when a husband was away or an older man had a young wife.
rows.anchor: ومنها القذف بالزنى وغيره من المساوي بدون مشاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet invited questions, many attendees wanted to ask who their father was, reflecting the practice of probing lineage.
rows.anchor: ولذلك لما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما ( سلوني ) أكثر الحاضرون أن يسأل الرجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: People cast doubt on Usama ibn Zayd's parentage because he was dark while Zayd was fair, but the Prophet affirmed his lineage as Zayd's son.
rows.anchor: وقد أثبت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أسامة بن زيد بن حارثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These false accusations were widespread in pre-Islamic society, and God prohibited Muslims from perpetuating their harm.
rows.anchor: فهذا خلق باطل كان متفشيا في الجاهلية نهى الله المسلمين عن سوء أثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being questioned is a metonym for accountability for neglect or transgression; here the senses are figuratively questioned when a person falsely attributes something to them.
rows.anchor: والسؤال : كناية عن المؤاخذة بالتقصير وتجاوز الحق ،

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A line attributed to Ka'b uses being questioned to mean being held accountable for one's deeds, supporting the metonymic sense.
rows.anchor: كقول كعب : وقيل إنك منسوب ومسؤول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense organs are imagined answering that they did not hear or perceive what their owner claimed, after which the owner is held responsible.
rows.anchor: أي يسأل السمع : هل سمعت ؟ فيقول : لم أسمع ، فيؤاخذ صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative أولئك refers to hearing, sight, and heart, treating non-rational senses as rational because they are the routes to, and substance of, reason; this usage is also conventional.
rows.anchor: تنزيلا لتلك الحواس منزلة العقلاء لأنها جديرة بذلك إذ هي طريق العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing responsibility directly to the senses is a rhetorical abstraction: their owners are what will actually be questioned.
rows.anchor: وفيه تجريد الإسناد مسؤولا } إلى تلك الأشياء بأن المقصود سؤال أصحابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a concluding summary of the warnings and prohibitions beginning at 17:23; every command entails forbidding its opposite, and every prohibition entails its contrary command.
rows.anchor: تذييل للجمل المتقدمة ابتداء من قوله تعالى : { وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read سيئة with a fatḥa and feminine ending, meaning the opposite of good.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور سيئة } بفتح الهمزة بعد المثناة التحتية وبهاء تأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the listed matters evil and disliked entails that they are prohibited or that their opposites are commanded; a commanded act would not be disliked by its commander.
rows.anchor: فالذي وصف بالسيئة وبأنه مكروه لا يكون إلا منهيا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage emphasizes what the items forbid because abandoning their harms is the chief concern; preventing harm takes precedence over securing benefits, though the two align here.
rows.anchor: لأن درء المفاسد أهم من جلب المصالح في الاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عند ربك modifies مكروها; placing the phrase first foregrounds God's judgment, heightens the censure, and implies that the person doing the disliked act is disliked by God.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { عند ربك } متعلق ب { مكروها } أي هو مذموم عند الله

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: These readers pronounce سيئه with a pronoun referring to كل ذلك; the explanatory genitive intensifies its evil as though the thing and its evil were two entities.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، وعاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف { كان سيئة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, what was forbidden is disliked by God; مكروها is best parsed as a second predicate of كان, fitting both readings.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون { مكروها } خبرا ثانيا ل ( كان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts back to the Prophet, recalling the opening command at 17:23; this is an intervening conclusion to the prohibitions and points to all the stated commands and bans.
rows.anchor: عدل عن مخاطبة الأمة بضمائر جمع المخاطبين وضمائر المخاطب غير المعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling these teachings wisdom encourages adherence; it honors the Prophet through revelation, since an unlettered person could not obtain such teaching unaided, and charges him to teach it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التذييل تنبيه على أن ما اشتملت عليه الآيات السبع عشرة هو من الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is knowledge of realities without error or confusion, and also speech that conveys such knowledge; compare its use at 2:269.
rows.anchor: والحكمة : معرفة الحقائق على ما هي عليه دون غلط ولا اشتباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed prohibition of associating a deity with God reinforces the opening monotheistic command and its warning of eternal, humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأكيد لمضمون جملة { ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ( الإسراء : 23 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Casting means throwing a body downward and conveys humiliation; the condemned person is blamed and expelled from God's mercy, and the subjunctive follows the prohibition with a causal fa.
rows.anchor: والإلقاء : رمي الجسم من أعلى إلى أسفل ، وهو يؤذن بالإهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the claim that angels are God's daughters, the Quran supplies sufficient guidance, yet the opponents turn further away from reflection.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر فظاعة قولهم بأن الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical sentence uses a waw of interruption; its pronoun refers to those who worshipped angels and called them daughters of God.
rows.anchor: والضمير عائد إلى الذين عبدوا الملائكة وزعموهم بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣrīf literally moves something repeatedly from one direction to another; here it means clarifying through varied forms of explanation, as at 6:46.
rows.anchor: والتصريف : أصله تعدد الصرف ، وهو النقل من جهة إلى أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ṣarrafnā is omitted because the verb is treated as intransitive: God made the exposition clear so that they might remember.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول صرفنا } لأن الفعل نزل منزلة اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليذكروا derives from يتذكروا, with tā assimilated into dhal because their articulation points are close; the root's sense is remembering rather than forgetting.
rows.anchor: ويذكروا : أصله يتذكروا ، فأدغم التاء في الذال لتقارب مخرجيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembered audience is inferred from the rebuke at 17:40, with a shift from direct address to third person or from addressing pagans to addressing believers.
rows.anchor: أي ليذكر الذين خوطبوا بالتوبيخ في قوله : أفأصفاكم ربكم ( الإسراء : 40 )

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read ليذكروا with a light consonant and a different vowel pattern, from the verb whose verbal noun is dhikr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف { ليذكروا } بسكون الذال وضم الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their increased aversion is a circumstantial clause intended to express amazement: clear, detailed discourse should reassure, yet they flee like frightened animals.
rows.anchor: وشأن التفصيل أن يفيد الطمأنينة للمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one interpretation, the omitted completion is that rival gods would contend for a route to domination; their struggle would disrupt the world, like the gods in Greek mythology, matching the mutual-prevention proof at 21:22.
rows.anchor: وتمام الدليل محذوف للإيجاز يدل عليه ما يستلزمه ابتغاء السبيل على هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under this interpretation, سبيل figuratively means gaining control and reaching the desired end, while seeking it implies hostility and rivalry.
rows.anchor: فالسبيل على هذا المعنى مجاز عن التمكن والظفر بالمطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase كما تقولون signals that their description of the alleged gods is erroneous.
rows.anchor: على هذا الوجه تنبيه على خطئهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, سبيل is a route of submission and approach to God: alleged gods would seek His favor, proving their dependence and contradicting divinity; compare the means of approach at 17:57 and the honored servants at 21:26.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالسبيل سبيل الوصول إلى ذي العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the second reading, كما تقولون limits the hypothetical to gods as the pagans described them, namely intercessors near God, as at 10:18.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration sanctifying God is an inserted conclusion to the proof in 17:42, refuting the claimed partners in divinity; comparable wording occurs at 6:100.
rows.anchor: إنشاء تنزيه لله تعالى عما ادعوه من وجود شركاء له في الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما يقولون encompasses all their claims mentioned earlier.
rows.anchor: مراد بما يقولون ما يقولونه مما ذكر آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: علوا is an absolute object in an irregular form, signaling rightful, real exaltation rather than mere pretension; a verse by Sa'da, mother of al-Kumayt, illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: جيء به على غير قياس فعله للدلالة على أن التعالي هو الاتصاف بالعلو بحق

rows.speaker: سعدة أم الكميت بن معر
rows.claim: Sa'da's line uses تعالى to describe rising above the truth, illustrating the distinction between genuine elevation and a claim to superiority.
rows.anchor: تعاليت فوق الحق عن آل فقعس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfect/complete sense of كبير underscores God's unqualified transcendence; necessary existence and permanence are incompatible with need, incapacity, partner, consort, or child.
rows.anchor: لأن وجوب الوجود والبقاء ينافي آثار الاحتياج والعجز

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use second-person تاء instead of the majority's third-person ياء, either as a shift in address or as part of the quoted speech beginning at 17:42.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف بتاء الخطاب على أنه التفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the worlds glorifying God is circumstantial to سبحانه: all created realms testify to His transcendence.
rows.anchor: جملة { يسبح له } الخ . حال من الضمير في { سبحانه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in له either marks transitivity of تسبيح understood as bearing witness to transcendence, or is the clarifying lām found in constructions such as الحمد لله لك.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { له } لام تعدية { يسبح } المضمن معنى يشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since many things that cannot speak are said to glorify, their tasbīḥ means that their state points to God's transcendence; people fail to understand because they neglect to observe that evidence.
rows.anchor: دل على أنه مستعمل في الدلالة على التنزيه بدلالة الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address لا تفقهون may target pagans who deny the transcendence creation displays, while believers can perceive it through Quran-guided reflection; alternatively, it addresses everyone because no one fully comprehends this glorification.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { لا تفقهون } يجوز أن يكون للمشركين

rows.speaker: فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din illustrates the point with an apple: each indivisible part and its specific qualities indicate a wise, powerful determiner, while their countless parts and qualities remain unknown to us.
rows.anchor: وقد مثل الإمام فخر الدين ذلك فقال : إنك إذا أخذت تفاحة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing تفقهون rather than تعلمون suggests that the denied knowledge is subtle and detailed, supporting Fakhr al-Din's argument.
rows.anchor: ولعل إيثار فعل { لا تفقهون } دون أن يقول : لا تعلمون

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: These readers recite يسبح with feminine plural تاء; both it and the masculine singular are permitted with non-rational plurals and nonliteral feminine nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو عمرو ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، ويعقوب ، وخلف بتاء جماعة المؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forbearance and forgiveness imply that the pagans' claim would otherwise merit swift worldly punishment; the verse urges them to desist so they may be forgiven.
rows.anchor: تعريض بأن مقالتهم تقتضي تعجيل العقاب لهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added كان presents forbearance and forgiveness as established, enduring attributes.
rows.anchor: وزيادة ( كان ) للدلالة على أن الحلم والغفران صفتان له محققتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the barrier مستورا intensifies its concealment, as though it were screened by another barrier; compare the emphatic phrase at 25:22.
rows.anchor: حجابا بالغا الغاية في حجب ما يحجبه هو حتى كأنه مستور بساتر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is an unseen barrier unlike ordinary screens; many reports say people who intended harm to the Prophet were thwarted, as in 2:137 and familiar sīra accounts.
rows.anchor: وقد ثبت في أخبار كثيرة أن نفرا هموا الإضرار بالنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of حجابا with مستورا is a rhetorical instance of antithesis.
rows.anchor: وفي الجمع بين حجابا } و { مستورا } من البديع الطباق

none: Verse text only; no commentary appears in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although they previously failed to understand the Quran, they grasped arguments that discredited their idols and turned away; they selectively ignore truth but hear what indulges them, deepening disbelief.
rows.anchor: فإذا سمعوا ما يبطل إلهية أصنامهم فهموا ذلك فولوا على أدبارهم نفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the phrase's apparent sense, وحده is a circumstantial qualifier of ربك: they resent that the Prophet mentions God alone and ignores their idols, which tacitly rejects them in context though mentioning one idol need not reject others.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( ذكرت ربك وحده ) ظاهره أنك ذكرته مقتصرا على ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means mentioning God as uniquely divine, which better explains their flight because they reject His exclusive divinity; وحده can describe reality or the wording of the mention.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن المعنى : إذا ذكرت ربك بتوحيده بالإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran-specific setting suits the discussion of listening, and the Quran's naming God without their idols implicitly denies those idols' divinity.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الذكر بالكون في القرآن لمناسبته الكلام على أحوال المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers why pagans crowd around the Prophet's recitation: they listen to catch claims such as monotheism and resurrection to mock one another, prompting the question raised by the preceding verses.
rows.anchor: كان المشركون يحيطون بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المسجد الحرام إذا قرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a new explanatory passage; beginning with the pronoun of majesty emphasizes God's complete knowledge of their motives.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الآية جوابا عن ذلك السؤال . فالجملة مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعلم means strength and detail of knowledge, not a comparison; the preposition باء links it to its object, while باء in يستمعون به marks association and its pronoun returns to ما.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد أن الله أشد علما من غيره إذ لا يقتضيه المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following إذ clauses clarify the otherwise vague ما; إذ is a time adverb for listening, and نجوى is a verbal noun used as a predicate to intensify their secret consultations, as at 4:114.
rows.anchor: والنجوى : اسم مصدر المناجاة ، وهي المحادثة سرا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ يقول is a partitive apposition to إذ هم نجوى, selecting one especially bizarre accusation because the Prophet's evident character contrasts sharply with that of a bewitched man.
rows.anchor: و { إذ يقول } بدل من { إذ هم نجوى } بدل بعض من كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them الظالمون rather than using a pronoun attributes their claim to wrongdoing: either their shirk, itself injustice, or their slanderous aggression against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن باعث قولهم ذلك هو الظلم ، أي الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a fresh opening; النظر signals that the matter is clear enough to see, and كيف expresses amazement at comparing the Prophet to a bewitched man and other figures.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام ب ( كيف ) للتعجيب من حالة تمثيلهم للنبيء عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضرب first means placing or fixing something and can mean shaping an object such as coins; here it metaphorically means presenting and clarifying an example, as in 2:26.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا مستعار للإبراز والبيان تشبيها للشيء المبرز المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in لك marks purpose: they fashioned a likeness of the Prophet; the idiom means likening someone to something, as also at 16:74 and 36:13.
rows.anchor: واللام في لك } للتعليل والأجل ، أي ضربوا الأمثال لأجلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural أمثال includes not only the cited bewitched label but their competing labels of poet, soothsayer, madman, and magician, reflecting their confusion and search for the nearest category.
rows.anchor: هو شاعر ، هو كاهن ، هو مجنون ، هو ساحر ، هو مسحور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misclassification is like forcing an unfamiliar animal into a familiar species, such as calling a giraffe a horse, camel, or cow.
rows.anchor: كمن يقول في الزرافة : إنها من الأفراس أو من الإبل أو من البقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضلوا may mean that their examples are false and deepen disbelief, or retain its basic sense of losing the way as they become perplexed about what to say.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالضلال هنا أصل معناه ، وهو الحيرة في الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to find a سبيل follows from their deep confusion: it may mean that they cannot find guidance, or compare them to a traveler lost in open desert.
rows.anchor: والسبيل : الطريق ، واستطاعته استطاعة الظفر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They keep changing descriptions because they expect people to disbelieve them and sense that each label contradicts reality.
rows.anchor: فلذلك جعلوا ينتقلون في وصفه من صفة إلى صفة

none: Verse text only; no commentary appears in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقالوا may attach to the earlier claim in 17:42, with intervening material as an aside, to refute another error; alternatively it continues the secret consultation of 17:47 before they publicize this argument.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون عطفا على جملة إذ يقول الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a denial; advancing إذا foregrounds what they regard as proof of impossibility, though it does not restrict resurrection to that state because every dead person becomes bones and fragments.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إنكاري . وتقديم الظرف من قوله : أئذا كنا عظاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿth means sending but here means reviving the dead because a corpse resembles one remaining motionless; عظاما are bones without flesh and رفاتا are finely crushed remains.
rows.anchor: والبعث : الإرسال . وأطلق هنا على إحياء الموتى ، لأن الميت يشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلقاً جديداً is a circumstantial description of the resurrected, intensifying the supposed impossibility; خلق is a singular verbal noun used as a result noun and therefore does not follow the plural.
rows.anchor: و { خلقا جديدا } حال من ضمير ( مبعوثون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply mirrors their كنا with كونوا and contrasts fragile bones with hard stone and iron, showing that God's power to reshape makes bodily weakness irrelevant.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الجواب أن وهن الجسم مساو لصلابته بالنسبة إلى قدرة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is not syntactically conjoined, following Quranic dialogue style; although قل introduces it, the command itself receives the force of an answer. Compare 2:30.
rows.anchor: لهذا كانت جملة { قل كونوا حجارة } الخ غير معطوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connection is puzzling because the skeptics objected to disintegration, not bodily weakness, so Ibn ʿĀshūr lays out three readings of the reply.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ارتباط رد مقالتهم بقوله : { كونوا حجارة } الخ غامض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, كونوا means that resurrection is equally possible whether they are dust, stone, or iron; this supplies an omitted answer and generalizes God's power. Then فسيقولون begins a new objection.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن تكون صيغة الأمر في قوله : { كونوا } مستعملة في معنى التسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, the command asks them to imagine being hard substances: they would still reject resurrection, and فسيقولون then shifts to another denial.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أن تكون صيغة الأمر في قوله : { كونوا } مستعملة في الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third reading treats كونوا حجارة as a new statement of equalization; the omitted premise is that even in this state they would ask who could revive them, extending their sophistry.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثالث : } أن يكون قوله : { قل كونوا حجارة } كلاما مستأنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iron is an earth-mined mineral found in varied forms and colors; the author describes eighteen types, rare pure iron, hard 'male' and soft 'female' varieties, products of smelting and forging, its susceptibility to rust, and broad availability.
rows.anchor: وأصنافه ثمانية عشر باعتبار اختلاف تركيب أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iron's hardness historically suited swords and armor; rust eats its surface, while heating and forging yield cast iron, wrought iron, and steel.
rows.anchor: فمنه ما يكون حديد صب ومنه ما يكون حديد تطريق ، ومنه فولاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The start date of ironworking is surrounded by unreliable stories, but people used iron before written history; rust explains the scarcity of surviving early tools.
rows.anchor: والمقطوع به أن الحديد مستعمل عند البشر قبل ابتداء كتابة التاريخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Archaeological scenes at Thebes and Memphis show tool-sharpening chests colored like steel in the twenty-first century BCE; Torah and hadith narratives about Abraham suggest the knife and circumcision axe were iron, and iron also made chains and maces, as at 22:21.
rows.anchor: وقد وجدت في ( طيبة ) : ومدافن الفراعنة في ( منفيس ) بمصر صور على الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلق means another created substance, such as steel or copper, that they considered too formidable to accept life; مما يكبر describes it, with greatness meaning strength and chests meaning minds.
rows.anchor: والخلق : بعنى المخلوق ، أي أو خلقا آخر مما يعظم في نفوسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted phrase means 'be things less receptive to life than bones and fragments'; if God can revive stone or iron, which never lived, reviving bones is easier still.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : كونوا أشياء أبعد عن قبول الحياة من العظام والرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فسيقولون follows the command: after being told to imagine these forms, they will ask who can restore them.
rows.anchor: والتفريع في فسيقولون من يعيدنا } على جملة { قل كونوا حجارة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They intensify the dispute by asking who will revive them, an argument by conceded premise after first denying resurrection's possibility; the Prophet is told to identify the first Creator.
rows.anchor: وجعل سؤالهم هنا عن المعيد لا عن أصل الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mocking question is answered literally to refute its implied impossibility: the one who first formed them can recreate them, as at 30:27; Moses similarly answered Pharaoh at 26:25–26.
rows.anchor: بقوله : { قل الذي فطركم أول مرة } إجراء لظاهر استفهامهم على أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause identifies the Creator and hints that His first creation proves His ability to recreate.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالمسند إليه موصولا لقصد ما في الصلة من الإيماء إلى تعليل الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنغاض is a repeated up-and-down head movement, here a gesture of mockery.
rows.anchor: والإنغاض : التحريك من أعلى إلى أسفل والعكس . فإنغاض الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their سؤال متى هو is mockery too; هو refers to the return implied by يعيدنا, and the Prophet must answer truthfully against its implication.
rows.anchor: وضمير { متى هو } عائد إلى العود المأخوذ من قوله : { يعيدنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عسى expresses hope on the Prophet's tongue that the resurrection may be near.
rows.anchor: و ( عسى ) للرجاء على لسان الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم يدعوكم may be a bound-time apposition to the hidden subject of يكون, with a built ending because it is attached to a verbal clause, or an accusative adverb modifying يكون.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ظرفا ل { يكون } ، أي يكون يوم يدعوكم ، وفتحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call may literally be made by angels driving people to assembly, or be God's creative command that revives and summons them to judgment.
rows.anchor: والدعاء يجوز أن يحمل على حقيقته ، أي دعاء الله الناس بواسطة الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding is a metaphor for obeying the summons and appearing for judgment; bones cannot hear or answer, so the imagery conveys instant resurrection and arrival without delay.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة مستعارة لمطاوعة معنى { يدعوكم } ، أي فتحيون وتمثلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may target the disbelievers who asked who would revive them and when, or believers in an alternative reading of the passage.
rows.anchor: وضمائر الخطاب على هذا خطاب للكفار القائلين { من يعيدنا } والقائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بحمده may describe those revived as praising God once they recognize the truth, or may be an omitted command for the Prophet to praise God at the vindication; on the believer reading praise is literal gratitude for faith and honor.
rows.anchor: فهم إذا بعثوا خلق فيهم إدراك الحقائق فعلموا أن الحق لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will think they remained only briefly; the astonishment at time's compression warns disbelievers and supports believers, as in the questions at 23:112–114 and the revival at 2:259.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا : أنهم ظنوا ظنا خاطئا ، وهو محل التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commands addressing pagans at 17:42, 50, and 51, the Quran turns to instruct believers, varying its topics to provide guidance for different people.
rows.anchor: ثني العنان إلى الأمر بإبلاغ المؤمنين تأديبا ينفعهم في هذا المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to use what is best is a general rule of speech and means varied expressions at the highest degree of goodness, not one fixed phrase; compare 16:125.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد مقالة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is closely linked to the preceding passage and needs no separate occasion of revelation; it disciplines careful speech.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية شديدة الاتصال بالتي قبلها وليست بحاجة إلى تطلب سبب لنزولها

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: In a sound report, the Prophet told Muadh that guarding the tongue is the key to the preceding good works, and that people are cast into Hell by what their tongues harvest.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح عن معاذ بن جبل : أن النبي أمره بأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chief aim is kind, gentle speech among Muslims, and restraint when debating pagans so harshness does not harden them or disrupt the vulnerable Meccan community; compare 41:34.
rows.anchor: والمقصد الأهم من هذا التأديب تأديب الأمة في معاملة بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبادي conventionally denotes believers; one report gives gentle formulas for pagans such as asking God to guide and have mercy on them.
rows.anchor: وروي أن قول التي هي أحسن أن يقولوا للمشركين : يهديكم الله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says pagans abused the Prophet's companions in word and deed; their complaint to the Prophet occasioned this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن الكلبي : كان المشركون يؤذون أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يقولوا is jussive with an omitted imperative lām, or a subjunctive answer to the command with the object of saying omitted; the latter implies ready compliance, as at 14:31.
rows.anchor: وجزم { يقولوا } على حذف لام الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh originally means a quick thrust and here means rapidly effective corruption, as at 12:100.
rows.anchor: والنزغ : أصله الطعن السريع ، واستعمل هنا في الإفساد السريع الأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about Satan explains the command: bad speech triggers discord, and بينهم refers to believers, advancing the law's aim of Islamic solidarity.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ضمير { بينهم } عائدا إلى عبادي

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi reports that a polytheist insulted Umar, who insulted him back and nearly killed him, risking a fitna; the verse then came down, though any occasion does not limit the general command.
rows.anchor: روى الواحدي : أن عمر بن الخطاب شتمه أعرابي من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's settled enmity dates from Adam's creation; he tempts believers to be harsh to disbelievers under the illusion that this serves religion, drawing them into evil while they think they do good.
rows.anchor: وذكر ( كان ) للدلالة على أن صفة العداوة أمر مستقر في خلقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects to the pagans' secret resolve and persistence at 17:47–48, consoling the Prophet who grieves over their refusal to believe.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك ينطوي على ما هو شأن نجواهم من التصميم على العناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best contextual reading takes mercy and punishment as guidance or being left to persist in error; other interpretations do not fit the verse's placement.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن ما تفسر به هذه الآية ويبين موقعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using your Lord, including the Prophet, recalls that selecting people for good belongs to lordship's care; the Lord knows their inner dispositions and what suits each person's condition.
rows.anchor: وأوتي بالمسند إليه بلفظ الرب مضافا إلى ضمير المؤمنين الشامل للرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعلم بكم means most knowing of your condition, since it is people's state to which knowledge relates.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { أعلم بكم } أعلم بحالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause explains God's knowledge; mercy and punishment signify guidance and misguidance while retaining their literal force, showing divine wisdom and that God is not questioned. The object of wish is omitted idiomatically.
rows.anchor: وسلك سبيل الكناية بهما لإفادة فائدتين : صريحهما وكنايتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction أو divides two mutually exclusive outcomes; repeating the condition stresses that God's will governs both and teaches His knowledge, wisdom, and freedom from compulsion.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالعطف بحرف ( أو ) الدالة على أحد الشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not a custodian responsible for forcing their faith: he is only a warner and caller, while God brings guidance or error, relieving the Prophet of blame for their refusal.
rows.anchor: أي ما أرسلناك لتجبرهم على الإيمان وإنما أرسلناك داعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكيل means one responsible for a matter; the denial entails the exclusive role of warner, and عليهم is fronted for emphasis and rhyme.
rows.anchor: والوكيل على الشيء : هو المسؤول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching verse endings الأرض and على بعض show that this is a paired passage, not an extension of 17:54.
rows.anchor: تماثل القرينتين في فاصلتي هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to 'your Lord' focuses on the Prophet after rebutting objections about divine attributes; pagans rejected him because he was not a tribal notable or leader, but God knows where to place messengership.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن المشركين لم يقبلوا دعوة النبي بغرورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal reference to all beings supplies a general premise for varied objections: whether messengers may be human, outside the elite, or unlike Moses, across people, angels, eras, and nations.
rows.anchor: لأن بعض المشركين أحالوا إرسال رسول من البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge grounds the selection and ranking of prophets, establishing that prophets existed before Muhammad and that people and prophets differ in rank; their rejection of him is obstinacy and envy, as at 6:124 and 4:54.
rows.anchor: فمنهم رسول ومنهم مرسل إليهم ، وإثبات التفاضل بين أفراد الصنف الفاضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr finds earlier explanations unsatisfying and notes two interpretive tracks: al-Ṭabarī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmit one from Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḥasan, while al-Qurṭubī and Fakhr al-Dīn give another without attribution.
rows.anchor: ومرجعها إلى طريقتين في محمل { الذين زعمتم من دونه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats 17:56 as an interlude between the favored prophets at 17:55 and the worshipped beings at 17:57: mention of true intercessors supplies an occasion to refute the claim that idols bring worshippers near God.
rows.anchor: والذي أرى في تفسيرها أن جملة { قل ادعوا الذين زعمتم من دونه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage reconnects with 17:42: that verse disproved rival gods rationally, whereas this one shows by experience that idols cannot remove harm.
rows.anchor: فبعد أن أبطل أن يكون مع الله آلهة ببرهان العقل عاد إلى إبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests the verse may have been revealed during Quraysh's seven-year drought, in response to the Prophet's prayer for famine like Joseph's years.
rows.anchor: ولعل هذه الآية نزلت في مدة إصابة القحط قريشا بمكة
